messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple container restarts detected on cluster=us-east-1, pool=model-serving-03. Symptom=CUDA OOM during prefill, restart_count=3+ within 2m. Severity=high. Paging oncall group: @ops-oncall.

maria: saw the bot — I'm grabbing logs now, will post stack traces. Placing immediate page to SRE handoff channel.

ops-oncall: on it. pinging runtime @liam and support @noah. Any customer impact yet?

liam: looking — preliminary logs show repeated kernel errors: "CUDA out of memory when allocating 24.0 GiB" during prefill for request_id=6a7f... Large context detected: client reported ~1.1M tokens (likely concatenated contents). Prefill loop grows KV cache until OOM triggers container restart.

noah: Support: one paying customer (acme-pay) reported elevated 5xxs around 18:04 UTC. I'm drafting a heads-up to them.

maria: quick triage notes: 
- Node metric spike: gpu_mem_used -> jump to 98% during prefill.
- Container crashloop with exit code 137.
- Kernel log snippet: `E Cuda: out_of_memory: tried to allocate 25.6G`
- Affected image: inference-runtime:v2.13.

liam: hypothesis: very long user prompt bypassed max_context guard due to legacy routing rule. Prefill allocates entire KV for sequence length before decode, so huge requests blow GPU.

maria: mitigation options (short):
1) add temporary per-request max_context=196k at our ingress/router for all hosted tenants (reject longer with 413)
2) enable fallback_worker=cpu for prefill on large-context route
3) patch runtime to evict prefix cache earlier (hotfix)
4) throttle long-context requests via WAF rule for 10m

ops-oncall: agree. Prioritize (1) + (2) immediately, + (4) while we bake a hotfix. (3) is next-day change but we can ship a config toggle to reduce KV retention now.

liam: applying temporary ingress rule now. Command:```bash
# add soft max context (hotfix)
kubectl patch configmap router-config -n redwood --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_context_override":"196608"}}'
```

liam: pushed the patch and reloaded router; returning 413 for sequences >196608 tokens. Monitoring.

deploy-bot: router-config updated (commit ad3f9c). 413 enforcement active across us-east-1.

maria: enabled CPU fallback for the long-context route: patched route to set fallback_worker: cpu for requests that exceed gpu-safe threshold. This will keep requests alive but increase latency/cost.

noah: sent quick customer note to acme-pay: "we observed transient 5xxs due to oversized request patterns; we've implemented temporary guards and fallbacks to prevent restarts. We'll follow up with root cause and mitigation timeline." They ack'd, asked for ETA on full fix.

liam: spinning up a small canary of runtime:v2.13-hotfix (evict-prefix-early) to validate KV eviction reduces steady-state GPU memory. Will test with synthetic long-prefill.

maria: monitoring now — memory spikes have stopped for new requests with the router guard. Existing crashloop pods are still cycling; initiating rolling restart of the pool to recover healthy instances. Command:```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime -n redwood --selector=pool=model-serving-03
```

ops-oncall: rolling restart started. Keep alerting rules muted for this incident to avoid noise, but keep the pager for new regressions.

liam: canary looks promising: KV peak reduced ~40% under same synthetic load using early-evict patch. Will prepare a patch release and coordinate with SRE for staged rollout.

maria: postmortem items captured:
- root cause: oversized prefill requests bypassed guard and caused unbounded KV allocation -> CUDA OOM -> container restart loop.
- immediate mitigations: ingress max_context enforcement (196k), CPU fallback for long-context route, WAF throttle rule, rolling restart of affected pool.
- long-term: add strict per-tenant request size limits, improve runtime's prefill memory accounting, amp up quantization heuristics for large contexts, and instrument per-request KV growth.

jess: CS: I'll follow up with acme-pay with an incident summary + timeline and offer a call if they want deeper technical detail.

noah: customer update queued. ETA for hotfix rollout to all regions ~3 hours after canary passes. I'll include mitigation steps and expected behavior changes (403->413 responses for very long requests).

ops-oncall: thanks team. Current status: mitigations active, customer notified, hotfix canary healthy. Keeping this thread open until full rollout. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident closed? No — severity downgraded to medium. Next update expected in 2h or after full rollout.
